title: Generic neighborhoods in a finite scheme stratification
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), and let $(a_j:S_j\hookrightarrow X)_{1\leq j\leq m}$ be a finite stratification by locally closed scheme immersions whose images partition $X$ [def-constructible-stratification]. The scheme structures of the strata are retained. The irreducible components $C$ of $X$ form a finite set, and each has a unique generic point $\eta_C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point]. For every $C$, let $j(C)$ be the unique index with $\eta_C\in a_{j(C)}(S_{j(C)})$. There is an open subscheme $W_C\subseteq X$ containing $\eta_C$ whose underlying set is contained in $a_{j(C)}(S_{j(C)})$. For the actual scheme fibre product $T_C=W_C\times_X S_{j(C)}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the projection $t_C:T_C\to W_C$ is a surjective closed immersion and the projection $q_C:T_C\to S_{j(C)}$ is an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The union $U=\bigcup_C W_C$ is open, dense, and contains every component's generic point. This asserts no factorization $W_C\to S_{j(C)}$. It holds without reducedness or irreducibility assumptions on $X$ or its strata; if $X$ is empty the family is empty and $U=X$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], the set $I$ of irreducible components of $X$ is finite: its hypotheses are exactly the locally Noetherian and quasi-compact assumptions on $X$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], each $C\in I$ has a unique generic point $\eta_C$, with $\overline{\{\eta_C\}}=C$. These assertions apply to arbitrary schemes, including nonreduced ones.

Fix $C\in I$. By the disjoint covering in [def-constructible-stratification], exactly one stratum image $A_C=a_{j(C)}(S_{j(C)})$ contains $\eta_C$. Since this image is locally closed, write $A_C=O_C\cap F_C$ with $O_C$ open and $F_C$ closed in $X$. As $\eta_C\in F_C$, the definition of closure and [def-sc-generic-point] give $C=\overline{\{\eta_C\}}\subseteq F_C$.

source.place: Tag 09XZ, definition-stratification; Tag 004X, definition-generic-point; locally closed means an intersection of an open and a closed subset

proof.text: Set $V_C=X\setminus\bigcup_{D\in I,\ D\ne C}D$. Each $D$ is closed by [def-weil-irreducible-components], and $I$ is finite by step 1, so $V_C$ is open. If $\eta_C\in D$, closedness gives $C=\overline{\{\eta_C\}}\subseteq D$, and maximality of the irreducible component $C$ forces $C=D$. Thus $\eta_C\in V_C$. Every point belongs to an irreducible component by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], so $V_C\subseteq C$. Consequently $W_C=V_C\cap O_C$ is open, contains $\eta_C$, and is contained in $C\cap O_C\subseteq F_C\cap O_C=A_C$. Give it the open subscheme structure of [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 004V, definition-irreducible-components; Tag 004W, lemma-irreducible (2)-(4); elementary finite-complement construction

proof.text: Put $S=S_{j(C)}$ and $a=a_{j(C)}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] to $a:S\to X$ and the open subscheme $W_C$. It exhibits $a^{-1}(W_C)$, with its original open subscheme structure in $S$, as $S\times_X W_C$. Swapping the two projections by the universal property in [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies this with the actual $T_C=W_C\times_X S$, compatibly with $t_C$ and $q_C$. Hence $q_C$ is the inclusion of that open restriction, so is an open immersion. For each $w\in W_C$, the containment $W_C\subseteq a(S)$ supplies $s\in S$ with $a(s)=w$; that $s$ lies in $a^{-1}(W_C)$ and hence gives a point of $T_C$ mapping to $w$. Thus $t_C$ is surjective in the sense of [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01JR, lemma-open-fibre-product, open-preimage specialization; Tag 01JP, definition-fibre-product

proof.text: The stratum map $a$ is an immersion by hypothesis. Its base change $t_C:T_C\to W_C$ is an immersion by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. Step 4 gives $t_C(T_C)=W_C$, a closed subset of the target $W_C$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] makes $t_C$ a closed immersion. Together with step 4 this proves the surjective closed immersion assertion while retaining the given scheme structures.

Let $U=\bigcup_{C\in I}W_C$. It is open and contains each $\eta_C$. Its closure contains $\overline{\{\eta_C\}}=C$ for every $C$, by [def-sc-generic-point]. Since those components cover $X$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], $\overline U=X$, so $U$ is dense. If $X$ is empty there are no irreducible components (irreducible subsets are nonempty by [def-weil-irreducible-components]); the empty family has union $U=X$, which is open and dense. All other assertions are then vacuous. No step uses reducedness or irreducibility of $X$ or of a stratum.
